title: Derived base change on the big etale ringed sites of stacks
statement: Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme] and an algebraic stack $\mathcal Z/S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], its big etale site has all objects and arrows of the fibred category in [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], with coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme maps. Its structure sheaf is $\mathcal O_{\mathcal Z}(z)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ for $z$ over $U$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $h:\mathcal A\to\mathcal Z$, direct image has value $(h_*N)(z)=\Gamma(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U,N|_{\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal Z}U})$; restrictions are induced by base change, and pullback of a module along a stack morphism means precomposition. Higher direct images are computed by injective resolutions in all module sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ and $b:\mathcal Y^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y$ be arbitrary morphisms of algebraic stacks over $S$. Form $\mathcal X^{\prime}=\mathcal Y^{\prime}\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, with projections $a:\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal X$ and $f^{\prime}:\mathcal X^{\prime}\to\mathcal Y^{\prime}$, using [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For every module sheaf $F$ on $\mathcal X$, placed in degree zero, precomposition $b^*$ and $a^*$ are exact functors on module sheaves, and the canonical base-change morphism is a natural isomorphism $b^*Rf_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\prime}_*(a^*F)$ in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y^{\prime}}))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Precomposition on complexes is termwise. Neither morphism need be representable, smooth, flat or qcqs, and $F$ need not be quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity] to each of $f,f',a,b$, with base the big etale site of $S$-schemes: every arrow of a category fibred in groupoids is cartesian, so these functors over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ preserve cartesian arrows, and the coverings of the statement are exactly the families lying over etale coverings. They are continuous and cocontinuous, so [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-topos-adjunction] gives morphisms of topoi whose inverse image is precomposition. The section rings agree, $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ on both sides at an object over $T$, with the same restrictions; hence [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-cocontinuous-ringed-restriction] makes them ringed-topos morphisms with identity structural map, and the tensor pullback $\mathcal O\otimes_{\mathcal O}(-)$ is precomposition via $r\otimes m\mapsto rm$. By the unconditional clauses of [lem-sfb-stack-representable-module-injective-transport] this precomposition is exact on module sheaves and left adjoint to the section-formula direct image, which is therefore the module direct image of these morphisms. Thus $a,b,f,f'$ give flat ringed-topos morphisms even when the stack morphisms are not flat. The $2$-isomorphism $\varphi:f\circ a\Rightarrow b\circ f'$ of the $2$-cartesian square gives the commutation isomorphism $H(\varphi_{x'}):H(b(f'(x')))\to H(f(a(x')))$ of inverse images; it is the identity on structure rings because $\varphi_{x'}$ lies over an identity scheme map. Actions on complexes are termwise. No representability clause of the cited node is applied to $a$ or $b$.

For $y'\in\mathcal Y'(V)$ put $C=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}(\mathit{Sch}/V)$ using $b(y')$, and $C'=\mathcal X'\times_{\mathcal Y'}(\mathit{Sch}/V)$ using $y'$. Expand the $2$-fibre products by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. An object of $C'$ over $T$ is $(t:T\to V,z',x,\alpha:f(x)\simeq b(z'),\beta:z'\simeq t^*y')$. Send it to $(t,x,b(\beta)\alpha)$ in $C$. The inverse sends $(t,x,\delta)$ to $(t,t^*y',x,\delta,\mathrm{id})$. One composite is the identity; the other is isomorphic to the identity by $(\beta,\mathrm{id}_x)$. These formulas also define the arrows and commute with their composition. They retain the scheme $T$, its maps, coverings, and section rings, and identify both coefficient restrictions with $F(x)$. For an arrow of test objects, both ways of restricting these formulas compose the same isomorphism $f(x)\to b(y')$ with that arrow. The direct-image section formula therefore gives a natural underived isomorphism $e_M:b^*f_*M\simeq f'_*a^*M$, linear over $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. It is the adjunction mate: the direct-image counit evaluates a compatible family at the object above $x$, and restriction along the displayed functor performs exactly that evaluation.

proof.text: Use the resolution-existence clause of [lem-sfb-module-resolution-derived-presheaf-comparison] on the two small ringed sites to choose nonnegative module-injective resolutions $r:F[0]\hookrightarrow I$ and $s:a^*F[0]\hookrightarrow J$. Exactness from Step 1 and the homology comparison of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] make $a^*r$ a degreewise monomorphic quasi-isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] to $a^*r$ with target $J$ and map $s$: there is $u:a^*I\to J$ satisfying $u(a^*r)=s$. Hence there is a chain map $v=f'_*(u)\circ e_I:b^*f_*I\to f'_*J$.

The complex map $v$ represents the canonical derived base-change arrow. Indeed bounded-below injective complexes $I,J$ are K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so their resolution units are isomorphisms by [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-ringed-exchange-resolution-unit] to $P=I$ and the exact horizontal pullbacks of Step 1: its equality identifies the canonical mate followed by the source resolution unit with $\eta^{f'}_{a^*I}\,Q(e_I)$. Naturality of this resolution unit for $u$ gives $Rf'_*(Q(u))\eta^{f'}_{a^*I}=\eta^{f'}_J Q(f'_*(u))$. Since $u(a^*r)=s$, the identifications by $r,s$ turn this equality into the assertion that the mate on $F[0]$ is $Q(v)$. Thus we have identified the prescribed morphism, before checking invertibility.

Fix $y'$ and identify $C'$ with $C$ by Step 2. The test-fibre projection $p:C\to\mathcal X$ pulls $I$ to an injective resolution $p^*I$ of $p^*F$ by [lem-sfb-stack-test-fibre-restriction-injectives] and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology]. The same node, applied to $f'$ and $y'$, makes $q^*J$ an injective resolution of the same module on $C'$. It remains injective after the equivalence: a lifting problem along a monomorphism is carried by the inverse equivalence to one for $q^*J$, and the resulting extension is carried back. The restriction $u_{y'}:p^*I\to q^*J$ preserves the common augmentation. By [lem-weil-pbc-lift-along-injective-quasi-iso] the augmentation into $q^*J$ admits a reverse comparison into $p^*I$. Both composites are homotopic to the respective identities by [lem-weil-pbc-lift-to-injective-unique-up-to-homotopy], since they agree on the common module in degree zero. Global sections carry these homotopies to homotopies by [lem-weil-pbc-homotopic-maps-equal-cohomology]. Under the section formula and $e_I$, $v(y')$ is exactly $\Gamma(C,u_{y'})$; it is therefore a homotopy equivalence and in particular a quasi-isomorphism. This uses injective preservation only for the two test-fibre projections, never for arbitrary $a$.

proof.text: Since Step 5 applies to every object of $\mathcal Y'$, [lem-pur-quasi-iso-of-sections] makes $v$ a quasi-isomorphism of module-sheaf complexes. All sites and modules are taken in the common small-skeleton universe of the statement. Localization therefore inverts $v$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Step 4 identifies this isomorphism with the canonical base-change morphism, which is natural in $F$ as the derived adjunction mate of [lem-sfb-flat-ringed-exchange-resolution-unit]. This proves the derived assertion as well as the exactness already established in Step 1, with all stated unrestricted hypotheses.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Projectivity of the unpointed stable coarse moduli scheme. Supporting input: Projective geometric quotients of closed stable loci for PGL. Affine-chart proof of the projective PGL quotient: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers. Supporting affine-quotient step: Finite inertia gives an adequate coarse moduli space. Supporting input to the finite-inertia coarse-space construction: Passage from invariant global power liftings on the affine rank charts to adequate moduli spaces, then etale descent to the glued map. Flat scalar-section comparison needed in the descent of a power lying in the image of a global algebra map; this does not assert adequate-moduli locality. General cohomological input: preservation of locally quasi-coherent modules and flat comparison maps under qcqs stack direct images. Supporting input: Smooth descent criterion for preservation by higher direct images. Supporting target-localization input to the smooth descent criterion: derived big-etale base change, without representability.

tool_uses.why: General uniqueness of comparison maps between bounded-below injective resolutions; the unit has no replacement for this homological algebra tool.
General ringed-site test that a sectionwise quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism, independent of purity; used on the big-etale module-sheaf complexes in the common universe.
General geometric morphism attached to a continuous cocontinuous site functor; makes the stack-morphism precompositions inverse images of topos morphisms.
General ringed-topos structure of such a morphism with identity structural ring map; needed for the ringed-topos square of the exchange-unit node.
